dana: Quick follow-up idea for cost attribution — introduce a tiny 'cost-hash' header that is deterministic and low-cardinality. Thinking gateway computes cost-hash from tenant id so downstreams can carry a stable billing tag without exposing raw tenant ids.

rick: Do you mean like hashing+bucket? How many buckets?

dana: Yes, deterministic bucket. Start with 256 buckets (configurable). Header: Cost-Hash: v1;bucket=042;src=gateway. Gateway computes murmur3(tenant_id)%256.

nina: Major ops concerns: cardinality guards and spoofing. If services can set header, they could misattribute.

dana: Plan: only gateways sign header (HMAC). Ingest prefers signed header for billing. Unsigned header is advisory and ignored for chargeback. Also enforce per-tenant bucket quota: if a bucket sees >N new keys/day, we collapse new values to _unknown.

rick: Sampling/order: we must read header before sampling decision so sampling keeps billing tag. Gateway must attach header early.

dana: Agreed. Also mirror (bucket,src) into trace metadata so queries can filter by bucket. We'll only index bucket (not raw tenant).

nina: Query surface: expose bucket column + resolve helpers for ops to map bucket->sample tenants for debugging. No auto-resolution in billing reports.

perf-bot: perf-runner: queued job 4623460500 'cost-hash-index-growth' (est 90m). Results to follow.

dana: I'll draft RFC with header spec, HMAC rules, bucket config, ingest caps, and rollout checklist. Tagging @eng-platform for review.
